text:
Jaden Schwartz is 34, playing about 13 and a half minutes a night in his first season in Colorado, and scoring like a man ten years younger: 7 goals and 13 points in 21 games. The first part is real. He gets to good ice, he still has a heavy shot (his hardest clocks in the top tenth of the league), and his 3.5 expected goals mean the looks are there.

The finishing is the part to hold loosely. Seven goals came on 3.5 expected, a 19% shooting rate against 13% last season, and the last ten games already show the drift: four goals, none in his last five games. We'd expect the goal pace to settle while the role stays useful.

What to watch is how Colorado uses him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 54% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so he fits a team that wants to turn pucks around fast. A third-line winger who can do that, with a 2019 Cup ring from St. Louis, is a nice thing to have even when the shots stop going in.
